docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
Step-by-Step Introduction to Mobile Programming with [Kotlin]

created by Anthropic’s AI Claude at the request of Serge Tahé - October 2026

|French version|

This course teaches you, step by step, how to write a native Android mobile app using the Kotlin language and Jetpack Compose, Android’s declarative UI library: an app whose screens are rendered on the phone based on JSON data from a server.

After setting up the development environment (Android Studio, emulator, Gradle), the course draws on 25 short examples, each focused on a single concept: activities and @Composable functions, state and recomposition, input fields, validation; component composition, their lifecycle, and their effects; CompositionLocal; animations; navigation (Navigation Compose) and its guards; coroutines, Flows, and shared state (ViewModel, DataStore); internationalization; and finally, communication with the server (OkHttp, cookies, kotlinx.serialization).

The server is treated as a black box: it is the JSON server for the RdvMedecins app, written with NestJS. We’ll set it up, study its API, and query it using 48 curl examples—without having to read its code.

Next comes a comprehensive case study: the RdvMedecins Android client, an appointment-scheduling app for a medical practice, with all files fully commented, followed by its deployment.

This course follows the progression of the “Step-by-Step Introduction to the Flutter Mobile Framework” course, using the same examples, server, and case study. Prerequisite: a basic understanding of the Kotlin language, as covered in the Kotlin course.

All courses by AI Claude and Serge Tahé

docs.title: 14. Appendices
docs.text: The installation of [Android Studio], the emulator, and the setup of a phone are described in the chapter “Setting Up the Work Environment.” These appendices supplement that chapter.

docs.title: 14.1. Using Android Studio
docs.text:
• [File / Open]: open a project ([exemples_kotlin], [rdvmedecins_kotlin]); [Gradle] “syncs” it (downloads the libraries);
  • the [Run] button (or Shift-F10) installs and launches the app on the device selected in the toolbar; [Debug] (Shift-F9) launches it with the debugger (breakpoints, variables);
  • [Apply Changes] replaces the code of a running application without restarting it, when possible;
  • the annotation [@Preview] on a parameterless function [@Composable] displays it in the editor, without an emulator;
  • the “Layout Inspector” ([Tools / Layout Inspector]) displays the component tree for the current screen and the number of recompositions for each component; “App Inspection” displays network requests ([OkHttp]) and databases;
  • Pressing Alt-Enter on an error suggests corrections (add a [import]...); Ctrl-Alt-L reformats the file;
  • Command line: [adb devices] (connected devices), [adb reverse tcp:8080 tcp:8080] (port 8080 on the device connected to the computer’s port), [adb install fichier.apk] (install an app), [adb logcat] (the phone log; in [Android Studio], the [Logcat] window), [emulator -list-avds], then [emulator -avd Pixel_8] (launch an emulator without [Android Studio]).

docs.title: 14.2. Screenshots from this document
docs.text:
The screenshots were generated automatically by INSTRUMENTÉS tests: [JUnit] tests that run SUR the emulator—within the same process as the application—and control it via the [Compose] test library (find a component by its text, tap it, type into it, etc.). They are located in the [app/src/androidTest] folders of the two projects: [Captures.kt] (a test function, for example) and [CapturesCas.kt] (a complete walkthrough of the application). An excerpt:

    @Test
    fun parcours() {
        langueFr()
        ActivityScenario.launch(MainActivity::class.java)
        pause(3000)
        seDeconnecter()

         // ---- the connection
        pause(1000)
        capturer("cas-01")
        saisir("Login", "admin")
        saisir("Mot de passe", "erreur")
        saisir("Recopiez les caractères de l'image", "test")
        bouton("Se connecter").performClick()
        attendre("incorrect", sousChaine = true)
        pause(1000)
        capturer("cas-02")

The scripts [outils/captures_exemples.bat] and [outils/captures_etude_de_cas.bat] launch the emulator if necessary, compile and install the application and its tests, set up the emulator (language, status bar in “demo mode”), run the tests ([adb shell am instrument]), and then retrieve the images. The JSON server must be started, along with [CAPTCHA_TEST=test].

docs.title: 14.3. Installing Node.js
docs.text:
[Node.js] downloads to nodejs.org: select version LTS (long-term support). The [Windows] installer also installs [npm]. It is only required for the JSON server. Verify the installation in a console:

node --version
npm --version

docs.title: 14.4. Installing MySQL with Laragon
docs.text:
The JSON server requires [MySQL] (or [MariaDB]). [Laragon] (laragon.org) installs a ready-to-use instance of [Windows] using the [HeidiSQL] administration tool. After installation:

  • the “Start All” button launches the [MySQL] server on port 3306;
  • the user [root] has no password: these are the default values from the server’s [.env.example] file;
  • in [HeidiSQL] (the “Database” button), the File / Run SQL menu item runs the [database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql] script.

For [Linux] or [macOS], install [MySQL] or [MariaDB] using the system's package manager, and run the script using the command-line client: [mysql -u root -p < database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql].

docs.title: 14.5. Installing curl
docs.text:
[curl] is included with [Windows] versions 10 and 11, [macOS], and most distributions of [Linux]. Check its version:

curl --version

The option [--json], used in this document, has been available since version 7.82 (2022). If you are using an older version, replace [--json @fichier] with [-H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @fichier], or install a recent version starting with curl.se.

In [PowerShell], you must enter [curl.exe], not [curl]: In [PowerShell], [curl] is an alias for another command ([Invoke-WebRequest]), which does not include the options from [curl]. The command prompt ([cmd]) does not have this issue.

docs.title: 6.1. Example 19: Coroutines, Flow, and Timers
docs.text:
Many things happen “later”: timer ticks, keystrokes, a server’s response. Where [Dart] has its [Future] and [Stream], [Kotlin] has the COROUTINES:

  • A [suspend] function can process ATTENDRE ([delay], a server response...) without freezing the phone: while waiting, the screen remains active. It returns a UNE value later: this is equivalent to a [async] function that returns a [Future];
  • a [Flow<T>] is a sequence of SUITE values over time, which are transformed using operators ([map], [debounce]...) : the equivalent of a [Stream];
  • a coroutine is launched in a PORTÉE ([LaunchedEffect], [rememberCoroutineScope], [viewModelScope]...); it becomes ANNULÉE when its scope ends.
// =========================================================================
// ex19/Ex19Activity.kt - coroutines, Flow, timers
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Many things happen “later”: timer ticks,
// keyboard keystrokes, a server’s response. Kotlin has the
// COROUTINES:
//    - a “suspend” function can ATTENDRE (a delay, a server’s
//      server...) without blocking the phone: while waiting, the screen
//      remains active. It returns UNE a value later;
//    — a Flow<T> is a SUITE of values over time (ticks,
//      inputs...), which are transformed using operators (map, debounce...);
//    - a coroutine is launched within a PORTÉE (scope): LaunchedEffect,
//      rememberCoroutineScope...; it is canceled when its scope disappears.
// Compose can display a Flow, recomposing itself for each value:
// collectAsStateWithLifecycle.
// =========================================================================
@file:OptIn(FlowPreview::class, ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::class)

import kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException

import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow

import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.flow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.map
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.mapLatest
import java.time.LocalTime
import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter
import kotlin.random.Random

val medecins = listOf("Marie PELISSIER", "Paul TATOU", "Sophie DUPONT", "Jacques DURAND", "Martine PELLETIER")

// A simulated “server”: a function SUSPENDUE, whose response arrives
// after a random delay
suspend fun rechercher(texte: String): List<String> {
    delay(200L + Random.nextLong(600))
    return medecins.filter { it.lowercase().contains(texte) }
}

// 1. A Flow created by the flow constructor { }: each emit ENVOIE a
// value to the collector
fun compteARebours(depart: Int): Flow<Int> = flow {
    for (reste in depart downTo 0) {
        emit(reste)
        if (reste > 0) delay(1000)
    }
}

fun heureCourante(): String = LocalTime.now().format(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm:ss"))

class Ex19Activity : ComponentActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        enableEdgeToEdge()
        setContent { ThemeExemples { PageAsynchrone() } }
    }
}

@Composable
fun PageAsynchrone() {
    val journal = remember { mutableStateListOf<String>() }
    fun tracer(message: String) = journal.add("${heureCourante()} $message")

     // the Flow is created UNE times (remember): otherwise, each recomposition
     // would restart the countdown!
    val rebours = remember { compteARebours(20) }
     // collectAsStateWithLifecycle: a state that tracks the Flow’s values
     // (null before the first one); data collection stops if the application
     // takes a back seat
    val reste by rebours.collectAsStateWithLifecycle(initialValue = null)

     // 2. Search as you type
    var saisie by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
    var resultats by remember { mutableStateOf(listOf<String>()) }
    LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
         // snapshotFlow: A flow of successive values for a Compose state
        snapshotFlow { saisie }
             // ANTI-REBOND: An entry is not submitted until 400 ms have passed without typing
            .debounce(400)
            .map { it.trim().lowercase() }
             // mapLatest: a new entry ANNULE for the previous search,
             // if it is not complete: no expired response
            .mapLatest { texte ->
                 // fewer than two letters: no search, no results
                if (texte.length < 2) return@mapLatest emptyList()
                tracer("recherche envoyée : « $texte »")
                try {
                    rechercher(texte)
                } catch (e: CancellationException) {
                    tracer("recherche annulée (périmée) : « $texte »")
                    throw e // a canceled coroutine must remain canceled
                }
            }
             // collect: consumes the values from the Flow, one by one
            .collect { resultats = it }
    }

     // 3. A value that arrives after one second: produceState triggers a
     // coroutine that PRODUIT sets a state
    val message by produceState<String?>(initialValue = null) {
        delay(1000)
        value = "trois (une seconde plus tard)"
    }

    val styleTitre = MaterialTheme.typography.titleSmall
    PageExemple("Exemple 19 - l'asynchrone") {
        Card(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
            Column(Modifier.padding(12.dp)) {
                Text("Un compte à rebours (un Flow, collecté)", style = styleTitre)
                Text(reste?.toString() ?: "...", style = MaterialTheme.typography.displaySmall)
            }
        }
        Card(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
            Column(Modifier.padding(12.dp)) {
                Text("Une recherche au fil de la frappe (anti-rebond, réponses périmées)", style = styleTitre)
                OutlinedTextField(
                    value = saisie,
                    onValueChange = { saisie = it },
                    placeholder = { Text("au moins deux lettres : pel, dur...") },
                    singleLine = true,
                    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
                )
                for (r in resultats) Text("• $r")
                if (resultats.isEmpty()) Text("aucun résultat", color = Color.Gray)
            }
        }
        Card(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
            Column(Modifier.padding(12.dp)) {
                Text("Attendre une valeur (produceState)", style = styleTitre)
                 // until the value arrives: the placeholder text
                if (message == null) Text("en attente...", color = Color.Gray) else Text("reçu : $message")
            }
        }
        Text("Journal", style = styleTitre)
        journal.forEachIndexed { i, ligne -> Text("${i + 1}. $ligne", fontSize = 12.sp) }
    }
}
  • lines 65–67: a simulated “server”: a suspended function whose response arrives after a random delay;
  • lines 72–75: a [Flow] created by [flow [ ... ]]: each [emit] sends a value to the one that collects it; [downTo]: a descending loop;
  • lines 96–100: the [Flow] is created UNE times ([remember]): otherwise, each recomposition would restart the countdown! [collectAsStateWithLifecycle] actually creates a state that tracks its values; garbage collection stops when the app goes into the background;
  • lines 107–125: search as you type. [snapshotFlow [ saisie ]]: the [Flow] of successive values from a [Compose] state; [debounce(400)], ANTI-REBOND: an entry is sent only after 400 ms without keystrokes; [mapLatest]: a new entry ANNULE replaces the previous search, if it is not complete: no expired response;
  • lines 119–121: a canceled coroutine receives a [CancellationException]: it can be traced, but must be restarted ([throw e]) for the cancellation to complete;
  • lines 130–132: [produceState]: a coroutine that PRODUIT a state (here, a value that arrives after one second).

On the left, at startup; on the right, after quickly typing “pel,” “du,” and then “dup”: only the keystrokes followed by a pause triggered a search, and the display shows the result of the last one.

docs.title: 6.2. Example 20: A shared state
docs.text:
A “store” is a state that spans HORS screens, existing as a single instance—UN—shared by everyone who reads it. Example 14 did this manually; [Android] provides the following for this purpose: an object created upon request ([viewModel()]), then rendered identically to everyone who requests it, and which is recreated upon a change in activity (screen rotation, language change). This is equivalent to the [provider] or [riverpod] packages from [Flutter].

// =========================================================================
// ex20/stores/Panier.kt - a ÉTAT PARTAGÉ, within a ViewModel
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A "store" is a state that exists across HORS screens, in a single
// instance, shared by everyone who reads it. Example 14 did this
// manually (CompositionLocal); Android provides the ViewModel for this purpose:
//    — an object created on demand, then rendered identically to
//      all functions of the activity that request it: viewModel();
//    - which is SURVIT when the activity is recreated (screen rotation,
//      language change): it is destroyed only when the activity is
//      permanently closed.
// Standard organization:
//    - the ÉTAT: a MutableStateFlow PRIVÉ, an observable value; externally, one
//      only see a read-only version (StateFlow);
//    - the ACTIONS: functions, the only ones that can modify the state;
//    - the calculated values: other StateFlow, derived from the first (map),
//      which do not change QUE if their value changes.
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.exemples.ex20.magasins

import androidx.lifecycle.ViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.SharingStarted
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.asStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.map
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.stateIn
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.update

data class Article(val libelle: String, val prix: Double)

class Panier : ViewModel() {
    private val _articles = MutableStateFlow(listOf<Article>())
    val articles: StateFlow<List<Article>> = _articles.asStateFlow()

     // DÉDUITES values: stateIn are actually StateFlow, which also exist
     // as long as the ViewModel (viewModelScope)
    val nombre: StateFlow<Int> = articles.map { it.size }.stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.Eagerly, 0)
    val total: StateFlow<Double> = articles.map { liste -> liste.sumOf { it.prix } }.stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.Eagerly, 0.0)

     // update: replaces the value with a new one, calculated from the old one
    fun ajouter(article: Article) = _articles.update { it + article }

    fun vider() {
        _articles.value = emptyList()
    }
}
  • lines 34–35: ÉTAT: a [MutableStateFlow] PRIVÉ, an observable value; externally, only a read-only version ([StateFlow]) is visible;
  • lines 39–40: DÉDUITES values: [map], then [stateIn], which in turn creates [StateFlow] that exist as long as [ViewModel] ([viewModelScope]). A [StateFlow] emits only if its value is CHANGE;
  • Lines 43–46: the ACTIONS values are the only ones that modify the state; [update] replaces the value with a new one, calculated from the old one.

For data to survive the application’s ARRÊT, it must be stored on the device. The [DataStore] library of [Jetpack] provides a small key-to-value dictionary, stored in a file specific to the application:

// =========================================================================
// ex20/stores/Preferences.kt - a state that persists after the application shuts down
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// For data to survive a shutdown of the application, it must be saved
// SUR The APPAREIL. Jetpack’s DataStore library provides a small
// key-value dictionary (Boolean, Int, Float, String...), specific to
// the app and stored in a file on the phone:
//    - reading is a Flow: it emits the stored values (read
//      asynchronously, without blocking the screen), followed by each new value;
//    - Writing is a suspended function (edit).
// No sensitive data (passwords, tokens) is stored there: they
// are written in plain text.
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.exemples.ex20.magasins

import android.content.Context
import androidx.datastore.core.DataStore
import androidx.datastore.preferences.core.Preferences
import androidx.datastore.preferences.core.booleanPreferencesKey
import androidx.datastore.preferences.core.edit
import androidx.datastore.preferences.core.floatPreferencesKey
import androidx.datastore.preferences.preferencesDataStore
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.map

// LE example preferences file: an extension property of
// Context, delegated to preferencesDataStore (only one DataStore per file)
val Context.stockage: DataStore<Preferences> by preferencesDataStore(name = "exemple20")

// what is stored
data class Reglages(val sombre: Boolean, val taille: Float)

class PreferencesUtilisateur(private val stockage: DataStore<Preferences>) {
    private val cleSombre = booleanPreferencesKey("sombre")
    private val cleTaille = floatPreferencesKey("taille")

     // what the device has stored; otherwise, the default values
    val reglages: Flow<Reglages> = stockage.data.map { p -> Reglages(p[cleSombre] ?: false, p[cleTaille] ?: 16f) }

     // an optional parameter named by preference: only what is provided is changed
    suspend fun modifier(sombre: Boolean? = null, taille: Float? = null) {
        stockage.edit { p ->
            if (sombre != null) p[cleSombre] = dark
            if (taille != null) p[cleTaille] = size
        }
    }
}
  • line 28: LE—the example’s preferences file: an extension property of [Context], delegated to [preferencesDataStore] (only one [DataStore] per file);
  • line 38: the read operation is a [Flow]: it outputs the stored values (read without blocking the screen), then each new value;
  • lines 41–44: the write operation is a suspended function ([edit]). Sensitive data (passwords, tokens) is not stored in JAMAIS: it is written there in plain text.

// AJOUTE to the shared shopping cart: the store does not LIT the shopping cart; it is
// not repopulated when it changes
@Composable
fun Boutique(panier: Panier = viewModel()) {
    Card {
        Column(Modifier.padding(12.dp)) {
            Text("Boutique", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleSmall)
            for (p in produits) {

// LIT the same shopping cart: only the quantity and the total (recalculated
// only if one of the two changes)
@Composable
fun ResumePanier(panier: Panier = viewModel()) {
    val nombre by panier.nombre.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
    val total by panier.total.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
    Card {
        Row(Modifier.padding(12.dp), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
            Icon(Icons.Default.ShoppingCart, contentDescription = null)
            Spacer(Modifier.width(8.dp))
            Text("$nombre article(s), $total €", Modifier.weight(1f))
            TextButton(onClick = { panier.vider() }, enabled = nombre > 0) { Text("Vider") }
        }
    }
}

// a LOCAL record (rememberSaveable), which disappears with the component...
// unless it is placed in a SaveableStateProvider (see Ex20Activity.kt)
@Composable
fun CompteurLocal(titre: String) {
    var clics by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
    Card {
        ListItem(
            headlineContent = { Text(titre) },
            trailingContent = { OutlinedButton(onClick = { clics++ }) { Text("$clics clic(s)") } },
        )
    }
}
  • Line 42: [panier: Panier = viewModel()]: the activity’s shopping cart, created on the first request. The store AJOUTE accesses the shopping cart without reading it: it is not regenerated when the cart changes;
  • Lines 60–61: The summary reads only the quantity and the total; it is regenerated only if either of these changes;
  • lines 75–76: a report (LOCAL), which disappears along with the component.

The screen:

// =========================================================================
// ex20/Ex20Activity.kt - three "ranges" of data
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//    - the status LOCAL of a component (CompteurLocal) disappears along with it;
//    - the state of a MAGASIN (the shopping cart, a ViewModel) is shared by all
//      components and survives their removal, and even a rotation of
//      the screen—but not when the application is stopped;
//    - the state stored on the device (preferences, DataStore) survives
//      shutdown.
// And SaveableStateHolder: it GARDE the local state (rememberSaveable)
// of content removed from the screen, and restores it if the user returns.
// Uncheck and then recheck "Show Area," then stop and restart
// the application: compare.
// =========================================================================

import kotlin.math.roundToInt

class Ex20Activity : ComponentActivity() {
     // lazy: the object is created on first use (the application context
     // does not yet exist when the activity is built)
    private val preferences by lazy { PreferencesUtilisateur(applicationContext.stockage) }

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        enableEdgeToEdge()
        setContent { Application(preferences) }
    }
}

@Composable
fun Application(preferences: PreferencesUtilisateur) {
     // saved preferences: null until they have been read
    val reglages by preferences.reglages.collectAsStateWithLifecycle(initialValue = null)
    val r = reglages ?: return // nothing to display before reading (a few milliseconds)
    val portee = rememberCoroutineScope()

     // dark or light theme
    ThemeExemples(sombre = r.sombre) {
         // text size: fontScale multiplies the text size by TOUS
        val densite = LocalDensity.current
        CompositionLocalProvider(LocalDensity provides Density(densite.density, fontScale = r.taille / 16f)) {
            PageEtatPartage(
                sombre = r.sombre,
                taille = r.taille,
                onSombre = { v -> portee.launch { preferences.modifier(sombre = v) } },
                onTaille = { v -> portee.launch { preferences.modifier(taille = v) } },
            )
        }
    }
}

@Composable
fun PageEtatPartage(sombre: Boolean, taille: Float, onSombre: (Boolean) -> Unit, onTaille: (Float) -> Unit) {
    var zoneVisible by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(true) }
     // the status manager for removed content
    val etatsGardes = rememberSaveableStateHolder()

    PageExemple("Exemple 20 - un état partagé") {
        ListItem(
            headlineContent = { Text("thème sombre") },
            trailingContent = { Switch(checked = sombre, onCheckedChange = onSombre) },
        )
        ListItem(
            headlineContent = { Text("taille du texte : ${taille.roundToInt()}") },
            supportingContent = { Slider(value = taille, onValueChange = onTaille, valueRange = 12f..22f, steps = 9) },
        )
        ListItem(
            modifier = Modifier.toggleable(value = zoneVisible, onValueChange = { zoneVisible = it }),
            leadingContent = { Checkbox(checked = zoneVisible, onCheckedChange = null) },
            headlineContent = { Text("afficher la zone") },
        )
        if (zoneVisible) {
             // removed: these components disappear, along with their local state
            Boutique()
            ResumePanier()
            CompteurLocal("État local")
             // also removed, but its status is GARDÉ set by etatsGardes, under the "counter" key
            etatsGardes.SaveableStateProvider("compteur") {
                CompteurLocal("État local, gardé par un SaveableStateHolder")
            }
        }
        Text(
            "Hors de la zone, un second résumé du MÊME panier (il reste là quand la zone disparaît) :",
            Modifier.padding(vertical = 8.dp),
        )
        ResumePanier()
    }
}
  • line 54: [by lazy]: the object is created upon first use (the application context does not yet exist when the activity is built);
  • lines 66–67: preferences are read; [?: return]: nothing to display until they have been read (a few milliseconds);
  • lines 71–79: the dark or light theme, and the size of the text (TOUS, [fontScale], and [LocalDensity]); Changing a preference launches a coroutine;
  • Lines 89–112: [rememberSaveableStateHolder]: a guard that GARDE saves the local state ([rememberSaveable]) of content removed from the screen, and restores it if the content returns.

On the left, two articles and clicks on both counters; in the middle, dark theme and hidden area: the summary outside the area still shows the shopping cart; on the right, the area redisplayed: the shopping cart is intact, the local counter has reset to 0, and the saved counter has returned to its original value. Stop and then restart the application: only the preferences (theme, text size) have been preserved.

docs.title: 11. Case Study: The Kotlin Client for the RdvMedecins Application
11.1. The Problem
docs.text:
The [RdvMedecins] application allows users to schedule appointments at a doctor's office. The [NestJS] course developed it as a HTML application, in which the server generated the pages; the courses [Vue.js], [Angular], and [React] developed web clients for it, and the [Flutter] course created a mobile client, which generates the MÊMES screens from the JSON data provided by the server described in the chapter “The RdvMedecins Server: A Black Box.” This chapter describes how to write a native [Android] client, in [Kotlin] and [Jetpack Compose].

The client must provide everything the others provided:

  • a login screen, protected by a CAPTCHA, with the option to create a patient account;
  • a doctor’s schedule for a given day, with appointment booking (patient selection window) and cancellation;
  • for the administrator, management of doctors and clients (list, add, edit, delete);
  • for the patient, a personal dashboard (showing upcoming appointments, which they can cancel) and account management;
  • two languages: French and English;
  • the same screens as the web clients ([/login], [/agenda], [/medecins], [/mon-espace]...), which here become ROUTES navigation screens.

A mobile app adds its own requirements: a narrow screen (no five-column tables), a keyboard that hides half the screen, a Back button, screen rotation and language switching that affect the activity (RECRÉENT), a password manager, and the absence of a browser to store the token cookie.

docs.title: 11.2. Installation and Execution
docs.text:
The JSON server must be installed and running (see the chapter “The RdvMedecins Server: A Black Box”). The CAPTCHA test mode is not required: you can leave the corresponding field blank in the server’s configuration file.

In [Android Studio], [File / Open] opens the [rdvmedecins_kotlin] folder; [Gradle] downloads the libraries (the first time, this takes a few minutes). Once the emulator is running, a command window connects its port 8080 to the computer’s port:

adb reverse tcp:8080 tcp:8080

then the [Run] button installs and launches the application. You can also do everything in a command window opened to the [rdvmedecins_kotlin] folder:

gradlew installDebug
gradlew installDebug -Pserveur=http://10.0.2.2:8080
gradlew installDebug -Pserveur=http://192.168.1.20:8080
  • The first line compiles and installs the application on the connected device (emulator or phone), which connects to the server at the address [http://localhost:8080] using [adb reverse];
  • the second, for the emulator, without [adb reverse]: the emulator sees the computer at the address [10.0.2.2];
  • the third, for a real phone connected via Wi-Fi to the same network as the computer: we provide the computer’s address on that network ([ipconfig] under [Windows]); the firewall on [Windows] must allow incoming connections on port 8080. A phone connected to USB (with “USB debugging” enabled in its developer options) can also use [adb reverse].

Demo accounts are listed on the login screen (password = login).

docs.title: 11.4. Client Architecture
docs.text:
rdvmedecins_kotlin/
├── settings.gradle.kts, build.gradle.kts    le projet Gradle
├── gradle/libs.versions.toml               les versions des bibliothèques
└── app/
    ├── build.gradle.kts                    le module de l'application
    └── src/
        ├── androidTest/                    le test qui fabrique les copies d'écran
        └── main/
            ├── AndroidManifest.xml
            ├── assets/i18n/                les dictionnaires fr.json, en.json
            ├── res/                        icône, nom, thème, langues
            └── java/fr/stahe/rdvmedecins/
                ├── RdvMedecinsApplication.kt  les objets partagés
                ├── MainActivity.kt         l'unique activité
                ├── Config.kt               l'adresse du serveur
                ├── Formatage.kt            les heures et les jours
                ├── api/                    la couche d'accès à l'API
                ├── etat/                   session, messages, cache
                ├── i18n/                   les langues
                ├── navigation/             les écrans, leurs routes, leurs droits
                ├── widgets/                le gabarit et les composants réutilisables
                └── pages/                  les écrans

This is the architecture recommended by the [Android] guide (“Guide to App Architecture”), simplified as follows:

  • a data layer ([api/]): the only layer that knows about [OkHttp], the URL objects, and the JSON object;
  • a state layer ([etat/]): objects whose properties are [Compose] states, created once by the [Application] object and provided to all screens ([LocalDependances]);
  • an interface layer ([pages/], [widgets/]): functions [@Composable], which display the state and transmit user actions.

The following table compares the HTML application from the [NestJS] course, the [Flutter] client, and this client:

Application HTML (NestJS)Flutter clientKotlin clientThe server renders each page ([res.render])Widgets render the screensFunctions [@Composable] generate the screens[views/layout.hbs] and its partial views[gabarit.dart] (a [ShellRoute])[Gabarit.kt], around [NavHost]the controller routes[go_router][navigation-compose], routes [@Serializable][JwtAuthGuard], [RolesGuard]The [redirect] function of the router[Protege] and a session-trackingthe token cookie, stored by the browsera client HTTP that manages cookiesthe [CookieJar] from [OkHttp]Flash message in a cookiea [ChangeNotifier], [Messages]a stateful class [Compose], [Messages]Dictionaries read by the server[Traductions] (JSON)[Traductions] (MÊMES and JSON files)language stored in a cookiein [shared_preferences]by [Android] ([setApplicationLocales])data that has already been read[Cache] (a few lines)[Cache] (a few lines, from [Deferred])Form rejected: the server reloads the page400/409 response, errors below the fieldssame

All of the client’s files are shown below. They are extensively commented; their comments are part of the course.

docs.title: 11.5.4. AndroidManifest.xml
docs.text:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- =====================================================================
     AndroidManifest.xml - la "carte d'identité" de l'application
     ===================================================================== -->
<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    xmlns:tools="http://schemas.android.com/tools">

     <!-- network access (server JSON) -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" />

     <!-- android:name: the Application class (RdvMedecinsApplication.kt).
         usesCleartextTraffic : le HTTP "en clair" du serveur de développement
         (à retirer pour un serveur de production en https, cf. Déploiement).
         localeConfig : les langues proposées par l'application -->
    <application
        android:name=".RdvMedecinsApplication"
        android:allowBackup="true"
        android:dataExtractionRules="@xml/data_extraction_rules"
        android:fullBackupContent="@xml/backup_rules"
        android:icon="@mipmap/ic_launcher"
        android:label="@string/app_name"
        android:localeConfig="@xml/locales_config"
        android:roundIcon="@mipmap/ic_launcher_round"
        android:supportsRtl="true"
        android:theme="@style/Theme.RdvMedecins"
        android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"
        tools:targetApi="33">

         <!-- the single activity. windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize": the
             clavier réduit l'écran au lieu de le cacher -->
        <activity
            android:name=".MainActivity"
            android:exported="true"
            android:windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize">
            <intent-filter>
                <action android:name="android.intent.action.MAIN" />
                <category android:name="android.intent.category.LAUNCHER" />
            </intent-filter>
        </activity>

         <!-- Before Android 13: AppCompat saves the selected language -->
        <service
            android:name="androidx.appcompat.app.AppLocalesMetadataHolderService"
            android:enabled="false"
            android:exported="false">
            <meta-data
                android:name="autoStoreLocales"
                android:value="true" />
        </service>
    </application>

</manifest>
  • a single activity, [MainActivity]: all screens are functions of [@Composable];
  • [windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize"]: when the keyboard appears, the screen shrinks (instead of being hidden by the keyboard);
  • [android:localeConfig] and the service for [AppCompat]: the application-specific language (see Example 21).

// =========================================================================
// RdvMedecinsApplication.kt - objects shared by the entire app
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Android creates the UN Application object at launch, before any activity, and
// keeps it until the app is stopped. It is created there, once for
// all objects shared across all screens:
//    - the client HTTP (and its cookie jar), the access layer to the API;
//    - the session (who is logged in?), messages, and the data cache.
// This way, they survive the recreation of the activity (rotation, language change
// language change). The screens retrieve them via LocalDependances (see
// MainActivity.kt): this is a hand-coded “dependency injection.”
// Two mechanisms link these objects together:
//    1. the 401 response to a protected request (expired session): we forget
//       the user and prepare the message; the navigation, which detects
//       the session, then redirects to the login screen;
//    2. A user change: the data retrieved for the
//       are no longer valid; the cache is cleared.
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins

import android.app.Application
import androidx.compose.runtime.snapshotFlow
import androidx.compose.runtime.staticCompositionLocalOf
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.ClientApi
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.RdvMedecinsApi
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.creerClientHttp
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.etat.Cache
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.etat.Messages
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.etat.Session
import kotlinx.coroutines.MainScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

class RdvMedecinsApplication : Application() {
     // a coroutine scope that lasts as long as the application
    val portee = MainScope()
    lateinit var api: RdvMedecinsApi
        private set
    lateinit var session: Session
        private set
    val messages = Messages()
    val cache = Cache(portee)

    override fun onCreate() {
        super.onCreate()
        val client = ClientApi(creerClientHttp(this))
        api = RdvMedecinsApi(client)
        session = Session(api)
         // 1. the session has expired
        client.onSessionExpiree = {
            session.oublier()
            messages.flash("ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED", succes = false)
        }
         // 2. the user changes: snapshotFlow transforms a Compose state into a Flow
        portee.launch {
            snapshotFlow { session.utilisateur }.collect { cache.vider() }
        }
    }
}

// the Application object, provided to all screens
val LocalDependances = staticCompositionLocalOf<RdvMedecinsApplication> { error("aucune dépendance fournie") }
  • Lines 35–41: shared objects, created once. [lateinit var]: a non-[null] property, initialized later (in [onCreate]); [MainScope()]: a coroutine scope that lives as long as the application;
  • lines 49–51: the session has expired: the function entrusted to the API client (which knows nothing else) forgets the user and prepares the message;
  • line 55: [snapshotFlow] transforms a [Compose] state into a [Flow] state (see Example 19): every time the user changes, the cache is cleared;

// =========================================================================
// Formatage.kt - the display of hours and days
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The server sends data BRUTES (start hour: 8, start minute: 0; day:
// "2026-10-05"); the formatting, which depends on the language, is the responsibility
// the client (see example 09).

package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins

import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.Creneau
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.CreneauAgenda
import java.time.Instant
import java.time.LocalDate
import java.time.ZoneOffset
import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter
import java.time.format.FormatStyle
import java.util.Locale

// "8:05" rather than "8:5"
fun heure(h: Int, m: Int) = "$h:${m.toString().padStart(2, '0')}"

// "8:00 - 8:20"
fun horaire(c: Creneau) = "${heure(c.hdebut, c.mdebut)} - ${heure(c.hfin, c.mfin)}"
fun horaire(c: CreneauAgenda) = "${heure(c.hdebut, c.mdebut)} - ${heure(c.hfin, c.mfin)}"

fun aujourdhui(): String = LocalDate.now().toString() // "yyyy-MM-dd", the format of the API

// true if the day is a valid date in the yyyy-MM-dd format ("2026-02-30": false)
fun estUneDateValide(jour: String): Boolean =
    Regex("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$").matches(jour) && runCatching { LocalDate.parse(jour) }.isSuccess

// "Monday, October 5, 2026"
fun jourLong(jour: String, langue: String): String =
    LocalDate.parse(jour).format(DateTimeFormatter.ofLocalizedDate(FormatStyle.FULL).withLocale(Locale.forLanguageTag(langue)))

// The Material calendar operates in milliseconds (UTC)
fun versMillis(jour: String): Long = LocalDate.parse(jour).atStartOfDay(ZoneOffset.UTC).toInstant().toEpochMilli()

11.7.1. API/ClientHttp.kt
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// api/ClientHttp.kt - a client HTTP that handles COOKIES
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from Example 23 (common/ClientHttp.kt). The server RdvMedecins
// places the token JWT in a cookie httpOnly. On a phone, there is
// no browser to store it: it is the “cookie jar” (CookieJar)
// of the client OkHttp that stores it and sends it back with every request. The
// cookies are also stored on the device (SharedPreferences): you remain
// logged in when you close and then reopen the app.
// Two cookies are in circulation: the token (rdvmedecins_jwt, path /api) and the
// account creation token (path /api/registration).
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api

import android.content.Context
import android.content.SharedPreferences
import androidx.core.content.edit
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.Config
import okhttp3.Cookie
import okhttp3.CookieJar
import okhttp3.HttpUrl
import okhttp3.HttpUrl.Companion.toHttpUrl
import okhttp3.OkHttpClient
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit

class CookiesSurLAppareil(private val stockage: SharedPreferences) : CookieJar {
     // cookie name -> the cookie
    private val cookies = mutableMapOf<String, Cookie>()

    init {
         // cookies stored from a previous session
        val base = Config.urlServeur.toHttpUrl()
        for (texte in stockage.getStringSet(CLE, emptySet()).orEmpty()) {
            Cookie.parse(base, texte)?.let { cookies[it.name] = it }
        }
    }

     // The response includes cookies: we store them; an expired cookie (the
     // the server deletes the token upon logout) is removed
    @Synchronized
    override fun saveFromResponse(url: HttpUrl, cookies: List<Cookie>) {
        for (c in cookies) {
            if (c.expiresAt < System.currentTimeMillis() || c.value.isEmpty()) {
                this.cookies.remove(c.name)
            } else {
                this.cookies[c.name] = c
            }
        }
        stockage.edit { putStringSet(CLE, this@CookiesSurLAppareil.cookies.values.map { it.toString() }.toSet()) }
    }

     // a request is sent: the relevant cookies, which have not expired
    @Synchronized
    override fun loadForRequest(url: HttpUrl): List<Cookie> =
        cookies.values.filter { it.expiresAt >= System.currentTimeMillis() && it.matches(url) }

    companion object {
        private const val CLE = "rdvmedecins.cookies"
    }
}

fun creerClientHttp(context: Context): OkHttpClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
    .cookieJar(CookiesSurLAppareil(context.getSharedPreferences("rdvmedecins", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)))
    .connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
    .readTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
    .build()

The client HTTP from Example 23, and its cookie jar. Two cookies are in circulation: the token ([rdvmedecins_jwt]) and the account creation pass.

// =========================================================================
// api/ErreurApi.kt - UNE handles all errors from API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Resuming Example 24 (common/ErreurApi.kt). All responses
// server error responses have the same format:
//    { "statusCode": 409, "cle": "ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN", "params": {...}, "fields": {...} }
// A request with no response (network issue, server down) or a response that does not
// comes from our server also become a ErreurApi.
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api

import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonObject
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonPrimitive
import kotlinx.serialization.json.jsonObject

class ErreurApi(
    val statusCode: Int, // 0: the server did not respond
    val cle: String, // e.g., "ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN"
    val params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
    val champs: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
) : Exception("$statusCode $cle") {

    override fun toString() = "$statusCode $cle"

    companion object {
        fun depuisReponse(statusCode: Int, corps: String): ErreurApi {
            val json = runCatching { Json.parseToJsonElement(corps).jsonObject }.getOrNull()
            val cle = (json?.get("cle") as? JsonPrimitive)?.content
            if (json == null || cle == null) {
                 // no key: the proxy or network responded instead of the server
                return ErreurApi(statusCode, if (statusCode >= 500) "ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE" else "ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR")
            }
            return ErreurApi(statusCode, cle, chaines(json["params"]), chaines(json["champs"]))
        }

        private fun chaines(json: Any?): Map<String, String> =
            (json as? JsonObject)?.mapValues { (_, v) -> (v as? JsonPrimitive)?.content ?: v.toString() } ?: emptyMap()
    }
}

docs.title: 11.7.3. api/ClientApi.kt
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// api/ClientApi.kt - TOUTES: Requests to API go through here
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from Example 24 (common/Api.kt), with one new feature: centralized handling
// Centralized handling of the 401 response.
//
// A 401 can occur at any time: the token has expired (2 hours), the
// account has been deleted, the server has restarted with a different
// secret key... Rather than handling this case on every screen, we handle it
// ICI, just once. But this file doesn’t handle navigation or
// messages (it doesn't depend on anything): it calls a function that was
// assigned to it at startup (onSessionExpiree, see RdvMedecinsApplication.kt),
// which forgets the user; the browser, which tracks the session, then returns
// to the login screen.
//
// Some requests handle their own 401 responses (login, GET
// /api/auth/moi...): these are “public” (see RdvMedecinsApi.kt).
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api

import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.Config
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonElement
import okhttp3.MediaType.Companion.toMediaType
import okhttp3.OkHttpClient
import okhttp3.Request
import okhttp3.RequestBody.Companion.toRequestBody
import java.io.IOException

class ClientApi(private val client: OkHttpClient) {
     // What to do when the server returns a 401 response to a protected request
    var onSessionExpiree: () -> Unit = {}

     // public: true for routes that handle the 401 themselves.
     // withContext(Dispatchers.Main.immediate): the function ends
     // TOUJOURS on the main thread—the screen thread—regardless of the caller’s thread
     // of the caller (in an application, this is already the case: nothing
     // changes; in an instrumented test, the caller may be elsewhere).
     // can therefore, upon return, navigate or modify the state without taking precautions
    suspend fun requete(methode: String, url: String, corps: JsonElement? = null, publique: Boolean = false): JsonElement? =
        withContext(Dispatchers.Main.immediate) { executer(methode, url, corps, publique) }

    private suspend fun executer(methode: String, url: String, corps: JsonElement?, publique: Boolean): JsonElement? {
        val reponse = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
            val corpsHttp = corps?.toString()?.toRequestBody("application/json".toMediaType())
            val requete = Request.Builder().url("${Config.urlServeur}/api$url").method(methode, corpsHttp).build()
            try {
                client.newCall(requete).execute().use { it.code to it.body?.string().orEmpty() }
            } catch (e: IOException) {
                 // no response: network down, server stopped, incorrect address
                throw ErreurApi(0, "ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE")
            }
        }
         // deconstruction of the pair (code, text)
        val (code, texte) = reponse
        if (code >= 400) {
            val erreur = ErreurApi.depuisReponse(code, texte)
            if (erreur.statusCode == 401 && !public) {
                 // Back on the screen thread: the state can be modified
                onSessionExpiree()
                 // the screen that was waiting for the response will also display the message CE
                throw ErreurApi(401, "ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED")
            }
            throw erreur
        }
        return if (texte.isEmpty()) null else Json.parseToJsonElement(texte)
    }
}
  • lines 42–43: the function exits TOUJOURS on the main thread, the screen thread ([Dispatchers.Main.immediate]): upon return, you can navigate or interact with the state without caution;
  • lines 46–53: the request, on the I/O thread (see Example 24);
  • lines 60–64: the new feature: a 401 on a protected route indicates an expired session. We process it as ICI, once for all requests: [onSessionExpiree()], then a [ErreurApi] whose key is the message to be displayed.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// api/Types.kt - the JSON objects exchanged with the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The translation, into Kotlin @Serializable classes, of the API described in the
// "The Server, a Black Box" chapter (see `commons/Types.kt` in the
// examples). Reading a JSON that does not have the expected format fails
// upon receipt.
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api

import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonElement
import kotlinx.serialization.serializer

enum class Role { ADMIN, DOCTOR, USER }

// POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/me, PUT /api/my-account
@Serializable
data class Utilisateur(val login: String, val nom: String, val role: Role)

// GET /api/captcha
@Serializable
data class Captcha(val id: String, val svg: String)

// a title, a first name, a last name
@Serializable
data class Identite(val titre: String, val prenom: String, val nom: String) {
    val libelle get() = "$titre $prenom $nom" // "Ms. Alice DURAND"
}

// a doctor or a client: GET /api/doctors, GET /api/clients/:id...
@Serializable
data class Personne(
    val id: Int,
    val version: Int, // optimistic lock: to be sent back with a modification
    val titre: String,
    val prenom: String,
    val nom: String,
    val login: String? = null, // only for ADMIN
) {
    val libelle get() = "$titre $prenom $nom"
}

// a time slot
@Serializable
data class Creneau(val id: Int, val hdebut: Int, val mdebut: Int, val hfin: Int, val mfin: Int)

// a calendar entry, with the DROITS of the logged-in user
@Serializable
data class CreneauAgenda(
    val id: Int,
    val hdebut: Int,
    val mdebut: Int,
    val hfin: Int,
    val mfin: Int,
    val libre: Boolean,
    val patient: Identite?, // null: available, or booked by another patient
    val moi: Boolean, // the logged-in patient’s appointment
    val reservable: Boolean,
    val idRv: Int?, // specified if the user can cancel
)

// GET /api/agenda?idMedecin=...&day=...
@Serializable
data class Agenda(
    val medecin: Personne,
    val jour: String, // "yyyy-MM-dd"
    val creneaux: List<CreneauAgenda>,
    val info: String?, // translation key (patient who already has an appointment)
)

// an appointment from GET /api/my-space
@Serializable
data class RendezVous(val id: Int, val jour: String, val creneau: Creneau, val medecin: Personne)

// GET /api/my-space
@Serializable
data class MonEspace(val patient: Identite, val rendezVous: List<RendezVous>)

// GET /api/my-account
@Serializable
data class MonCompte(val titre: String, val prenom: String, val nom: String, val login: String, val version: Int)

val jsonApi = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }

// JsonElement -> Kotlin object
inline fun <reified T> JsonElement?.lire(): T =
    jsonApi.decodeFromJsonElement(serializer<T>(), this ?: throw IllegalStateException("réponse vide"))

docs.title: 11.7.5. api/RdvMedecinsApi.kt
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// api/RdvMedecinsApi.kt - a function per route from API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The client’s “data access layer” (a “repository”): the screens
// call these typed functions without knowing anything about URL, OkHttp, or
// or JSON. If API changes, only this file changes.
// Each function is suspended; if it fails, it triggers a ErreurApi.
// The form data consists of simple Map<String, Any?> : leurs
// The keys are the field names expected by the server—and those of the
// errors it returns (ErreurApi.champs).
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api

import android.net.Uri
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonElement
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonNull
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonObject
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonPrimitive
import kotlinx.serialization.json.boolean
import kotlinx.serialization.json.jsonObject
import kotlinx.serialization.json.jsonPrimitive

// /api/doctors or /api/clients: both are handled the same way
enum class TypePersonnes(val chemin: String) { MEDECINS("medecins"), CLIENTS("clients") }

typealias Donnees = Map<String, Any?>

// form data -> a JSON object
fun Donnees.versJson(): JsonObject = JsonObject(
    mapValues { (_, v) ->
        when (v) {
            null -> JsonNull
            is Number -> JsonPrimitive(v)
            is Boolean -> JsonPrimitive(v)
            else -> JsonPrimitive(v.toString())
        }
    },
)

class RdvMedecinsApi(private val client: ClientApi) {
    private suspend fun get(url: String, publique: Boolean = false) = client.requete("GET", url, publique = publique)

    private suspend fun post(url: String, corps: JsonElement, publique: Boolean = false) =
        client.requete("POST", url, corps, publique)

     // ------------------------------------------------ login (public routes)
    suspend fun captcha(): Captcha = get("/captcha", publique = true).lire()

    suspend fun moi(): Utilisateur = get("/auth/moi", publique = true).lire()

    suspend fun connecter(login: String, password: String, captchaId: String, captcha: String): Utilisateur =
        post(
            "/auth/login",
            mapOf("login" to login, "password" to password, "captchaId" to captchaId, "captcha" to captcha).versJson(),
            publique = true,
        ).lire()

    suspend fun deconnecter() {
        post("/auth/logout", JsonObject(emptyMap()), publique = true)
    }

     // ------------------------------------------------ account creation (public)
    suspend fun accesInscription(captchaId: String, captcha: String) {
        post("/inscription/acces", mapOf("captchaId" to captchaId, "captcha" to captcha).versJson(), publique = true)
    }

    suspend fun etatAccesInscription(): Boolean =
        get("/inscription/acces", publique = true)?.jsonObject?.get("valide")?.jsonPrimitive?.boolean ?: false

     // returns the login for the created account
    suspend fun inscrire(donnees: Donnees): String =
        post("/inscription", donnees.versJson(), publique = true)!!.jsonObject["login"]!!.jsonPrimitive.content

     // ------------------------------------------------ calendar and appointments
     // idMedecin null: for a connected doctor, SON calendar
    suspend fun agenda(idMedecin: Int?, jour: String): Agenda {
        val parametres = Uri.Builder().appendQueryParameter("jour", jour).apply {
            if (idMedecin != null) appendQueryParameter("idMedecin", "$idMedecin")
        }.build().encodedQuery
        return get("/agenda?$parametres").lire()
    }

    suspend fun reserver(jour: String, idCreneau: Int, idClient: Int?) {
        post("/rendez-vous", buildMap { put("jour", jour); put("idCreneau", idCreneau); if (idClient != null) put("idClient", idClient) }.versJson())
    }

    suspend fun annulerRv(idRv: Int) {
        client.requete("DELETE", "/rendez-vous/$idRv")
    }

     // ------------------------------------------------ doctors and patients
    suspend fun lister(type: TypePersonnes): List<Personne> = get("/${type.chemin}").lire()

    suspend fun lire(type: TypePersonnes, id: Int): Personne = get("/${type.chemin}/$id").lire()

    suspend fun ajouter(type: TypePersonnes, donnees: Donnees): Personne = post("/${type.chemin}", donnees.versJson()).lire()

    suspend fun modifier(type: TypePersonnes, id: Int, donnees: Donnees): Personne =
        client.requete("PUT", "/${type.chemin}/$id", donnees.versJson()).lire()

    suspend fun supprimer(type: TypePersonnes, id: Int) {
        client.requete("DELETE", "/${type.chemin}/$id")
    }

     // ------------------------------------------------ Patient Area
    suspend fun monEspace(): MonEspace = get("/mon-espace").lire()

    suspend fun monCompte(): MonCompte = get("/mon-compte").lire()

    suspend fun modifierMonCompte(donnees: Donnees): Utilisateur = client.requete("PUT", "/mon-compte", donnees.versJson()).lire()

    suspend fun supprimerMonCompte(motDePasseActuel: String) {
        client.requete("DELETE", "/mon-compte", mapOf("motDePasseActuel" to motDePasseActuel).versJson())
    }
}
  • line 24: doctors or clients: an enumeration, with the path to the API for each;
  • lines 26–29: form data: a [Map] whose keys are the names of the fields expected by the server, converted to JSON;
  • lines 40–110: one function per route of the API, grouped by theme; the routes that handle the 401 themselves are “public.”

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from Example 25 (Dictionnaire.kt). The dictionaries
// (assets/i18n/fr.json, en.json) are those used by the Vue.js and Angular clients,
// React, and Flutter clients: same keys, same conventions ({{param}}). The server
// returns only CLÉS ("ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN"): this is where they
// become text.
//    - t("CLE", mapOf("param" to value)): the text for the current language;
//    - changerLangue("en"): the language PROPRE in the app (see example
//      21), stored by Android; the activity is recreated in the new
//      language: our texts, as well as those from Android (the calendar), the
//      dates, and numbers.
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.i18n

import android.content.Context
import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatDelegate
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.staticCompositionLocalOf
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalConfiguration
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalContext
import androidx.core.os.LocaleListCompat
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonElement
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonObject
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonPrimitive

val langues = listOf("fr", "en")

class Traductions(context: Context, val langue: String) {
    private val racine: JsonObject = context.assets.open("i18n/$langue.json").bufferedReader().use {
        Json.parseToJsonElement(it.readText()) as JsonObject
    }

     // "LOGIN.TITLE" -> rootQZXW2HTMLBWyJMT0dJTiJdZQXQZXW2HTMLBWyJUSVRMRSJdZQX; null if absent
    private fun chercher(cle: String): String? {
        var noeud: JsonElement? = racine
        for (partie in cle.split('.')) noeud = (noeud as? JsonObject)?.get(partie)
        return (noeud as? JsonPrimitive)?.takeIf { it.isString }?.content
    }

     // an unknown key is displayed as-is: you can immediately see what’s missing
    fun t(cle: String, params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap()): String {
        val texte = chercher(cle) ?: return cle
        return Regex("\\{\\{(\\w+)\\}\\}").replace(texte) { m -> params[m.groupValues[1]] ?: m.value }
    }
}

// the application language: Android stores it and recreates the activity
fun changerLangue(langue: String) {
    AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales(LocaleListCompat.forLanguageTags(langue))
}

// translations, provided for all screens (see MainActivity.kt)
val LocalTraductions = staticCompositionLocalOf<Traductions> { error("aucune traduction fournie") }

// translations for the current configuration language
@Composable
fun rememberTraductions(): Traductions {
    val context = LocalContext.current
    val langue = LocalConfiguration.current.locales[0].language.let { if (it in langues) it else "fr" }
    return remember(langue) { Traductions(context, langue) }
}

// a shortcut in a @Composable function: t("LOGIN.TITLE")
@Composable
fun t(cle: String, params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap()): String = LocalTraductions.current.t(cle, params)

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// state/Session.kt - Is QUI logged in?
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The logged-in user (or null), in a state observed by Compose
// (mutableStateOf): the screens that read it are recomposed when it
// changes, and navigation (see navigation/Navigation.kt) observes it to
// exit a screen that is no longer permitted.
//
// The JWT token itself is not PAS here: it is stored in a cookie by
// the client HTTP. The session stores only the user’s DESCRIPTION
// ({ login, name, role }).
//
// When the application starts, the session is empty: `verifier()` sends
// the server—only once—to check which user is logged in (GET /api/auth/moi).
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.etat

import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.RdvMedecinsApi
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.Role
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.Utilisateur

class Session(private val api: RdvMedecinsApi) {
    var utilisateur by mutableStateOf<Utilisateur?>(null)
        private set

     // true after logging out VOULUE (button, account deletion);
     // false after a session has expired. Navigation takes this into account
    var departVolontaire = false
        private set

     // the screen we wanted to see when the session expired (a route):
     // we’ll return to this after logging in
    var ecranDemande: Any? = null

     // the displayed screen (a route), recorded by each protected screen
    var ecranCourant: Any? = null

     // Has the question “Who is logged in?” already been asked?
    var verifiee by mutableStateOf(false)
        private set

     // only queries the server the first time
    suspend fun verifier() {
        if (verifiee) return
        utilisateur = try {
            api.moi()
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            null // 401: No one; or server unreachable
        }
        verifiee = true
    }

    suspend fun connecter(login: String, password: String, captchaId: String, captcha: String) {
        changer(api.connecter(login, password, captchaId, captcha))
    }

     // The user has changed their name or login (PUT /api/my-account)
    fun mettreAJour(u: Utilisateur) = changer(u)

    suspend fun deconnecter() {
        try {
            api.deconnecter()
        } finally {
            oublier(volontaire = true) // even if the server does not respond
        }
    }

     // without making a request to the server: session expired, account deleted
    fun oublier(volontaire: Boolean = false) = changer(null, volontaire)

    private fun changer(u: Utilisateur?, volontaire: Boolean = false) {
        departVolontaire = volontaire
        utilisateur = u
    }
}

// What we can infer about the user: properties of EXTENSION such as
// User? (they also apply to null)
val Utilisateur?.estAdmin get() = this?.role == Role.ADMIN
val Utilisateur?.estPatient get() = this?.role == Role.USER

// ADMIN and DOCTOR: schedule and cancel appointments for any patient
val Utilisateur?.estGestionnaire get() = this?.role == Role.ADMIN || this?.role == Role.DOCTOR

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// status/Messages.kt - messages displayed to the user
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Same layout as other clients of RdvMedecins:
//    - a SUCCÈS is displayed as HAUT on the screen (green banner);
//    - a ERREUR appears as BAS (pink banner), which remains visible.
// A message is a translation CLÉ (+ its settings): it is therefore re-translated
// on its own if the user changes the language.
//
// "Flash" messages: an action that ends with a change
// (reservation, adding a doctor, etc.) places its message with
// flash(); it will appear on the SUIVANT screen, then disappear upon
// next screen transition. It is the navigation that calls nouvellePage() at
// every time the screen changes (see navigation/Navigation.kt).
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.etat

import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.ErreurApi

data class Message(val cle: String, val params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap())

class Messages {
    var succes by mutableStateOf<Message?>(null)
        private set
    var erreur by mutableStateOf<Message?>(null)
        private set

     // the messages to be displayed on the next screen
    private var succesEnAttente: Message? = null
    private var erreurEnAttente: Message? = null

    fun afficherSucces(cle: String, params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap()) {
        succes = Message(cle, params)
        erreur = null
    }

    fun afficherErreur(cle: String, params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap()) {
        erreur = Message(cle, params)
        succes = null
    }

    fun afficherErreurApi(e: ErreurApi) = afficherErreur(e.cle, e.params)

    fun effacer() {
        succes = null
        erreur = null
    }

     // for screen SUIVANT
    fun flash(cle: String, params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), succes: Boolean = true) {
        if (succes) succesEnAttente = Message(cle, params) else erreurEnAttente = Message(cle, params)
    }

     // a new screen: the messages from the previous screen disappear, the
     // flash messages appear
    fun nouvellePage() {
        succes = succesEnAttente
        erreur = erreurEnAttente
        succesEnAttente = null
        erreurEnAttente = null
    }
}

docs.title: 11.9.3. status/Cache.kt
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// status/Cache.kt - data already read from the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The list of doctors hardly ever changes: no need to reload it
// every time you visit the calendar. The cache stores the result of each read,
// under a CLÉ ("doctors", "calendar/1/2026-10-05"...) :
//
//      val doctors = cache.lire("doctors") { api.lister(TypePersonnes.MEDECINS) }
//
// returns the result already stored, or initiates the read operation and stores its
// result. Two simultaneous requests for the same key share the same
// read (a Deferred: a result to come). A failed read is
// not cached: the next request will retry.
// After a modification, the affected keys are INVALIDE:
// cache.invalider("agenda"). The version property, an observed state,
// then changes: the screens that read it (even if hidden behind another window)
// reload their data. In a nutshell, this is what the
// TanStack Query library in the React client.
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.etat

import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.Deferred
import kotlinx.coroutines.async

class Cache(private val portee: CoroutineScope) {
    private val lectures = mutableMapOf<String, Deferred<Any?>>()

    var version by mutableIntStateOf(0)
        private set

    @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
    suspend fun <T> lire(cle: String, charger: suspend () -> T): T {
        val lecture = lectures.getOrPut(cle) { portee.async { charger() } }
        try {
            return lecture.await() as T
        } catch (e: Exception) {
             // If it fails, this read is ignored (the next request will try again)
            if (lectures[cle] === lecture) lectures.remove(cle)
            throw e
        }
    }

     // ignores all keys that start with the prefix and notifies the screens
    fun invalider(prefixe: String) {
        lectures.keys.removeAll { it.startsWith(prefixe) }
        version++
    }

     // User change: everything is discarded; SANS notify (the screens from
     // the previous user will disappear; they must not re-read anything)
    fun vider() = lectures.clear()
}
  • Lines 36–39: [getOrPut]: If a read operation has already been started for this key, continue with that one; otherwise, start a new one. [async] launches a coroutine that produces a [Deferred], a result to come: two simultaneous requests are waiting ([await]) for the MÊME read;
  • Lines 48–50: [invalider]: The screens that read [version] from the key of a [LaunchedEffect] re-read their data.

// =========================================================================
// navigation/Ecrans.kt - the ROUTES of the application (see example 17)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The same screens as other clients (/login, /calendar, /doctors,
// /my-space...), described by @Serializable Kotlin objects, stored
// in an Ecrans object: Ecrans.Agenda(idMedecin = 1, day = "2026-10-05").
// TOUT the status of a screen is in its path (doctor, day...): the
// The phone’s Back button restores it exactly as it was.
// The appointment window is also a route (Ecrans.Reservation):
// a “dialog” destination, displayed as PAR-DESSUS in the calendar; the
// the Back button closes it.
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.navigation

import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.Role
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.TypePersonnes
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.Utilisateur
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

object Ecrans {
     // the first screen: time to ask the server which one is connected
    @Serializable
    object Demarrage

     // login: pre-filled immediately after creating an account
    @Serializable
    data class Login(val login: String = "")

     // day: as-is, may be invalid (it is verified by the screen)
    @Serializable
    data class Agenda(val idMedecin: Int? = null, val jour: String? = null)

    @Serializable
    data class Reservation(val idMedecin: Int?, val jour: String, val idCreneau: Int)

     // screens for managing doctors OU and clients (ADMIN)
    @Serializable
    data class Personnes(val type: TypePersonnes)

     // ID null: creation; otherwise, modification
    @Serializable
    data class Personne(val type: TypePersonnes, val id: Int? = null)

    @Serializable
    object Inscription

    @Serializable
    object MonEspace

    @Serializable
    object MonCompte
}

// roles permitted for a protected screen (null: all logged-in roles)
val rolesAdmin = setOf(Role.ADMIN)
val rolesPatient = setOf(Role.USER)

// the home page for each role, immediately after login
fun accueil(u: Utilisateur): Any = if (u.role == Role.USER) Ecrans.MonEspace else Ecrans.Agenda()

The application’s navigation paths, organized in a [Ecrans] object. TOUT: A screen’s state is stored in its navigation path; the phone’s Back button restores it exactly as it was. The reservation window is also a navigation path.
